title: W-27 to W-32: state Ward's limits in the README (TTY check, same-user authority, rollback, no forensic deletion, ad-hoc identity, checksums)
description: Source: the consolidated pre-public security review (opum-doc, 2026-10-30), reviewed at b1dae53374a8c0c3514f015ff77faac9af643e2d; tracked under ODOC-552 and parent WCLI-95. Report id: W-27, W-28, W-29, W-30, W-31, W-32. These are accepted design limits, not defects, and publishing without stating them is the one documentation gap that matters. The README must say plainly: a TTY check is not authentication and a same-user agent can supply a pty, approve its own profile and export a backup (W-27); Ward is not a security boundary against an agent with your full OS authority (W-28); integrity detects modified ciphertext, not an older valid one (W-29); zeroing is best effort, deletion is not forensic, and audit is operator convenience not an attestation, with a 500-event ring across the vault (W-30); expect one keychain approval after each upgrade and check the dialog names the installed binary (W-31); the checks detect a corrupted download, not a compromised release (W-32).

acceptanceCriteria.text: The README states each of the six limits plainly
The statements agree with spec 4.2 and 4.3 and ADRs 0001, 0002, 0003 and 0006
